Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> The global polypropylene market is estimated to be valued at USD 125.62 billion in 2025; The global polypropylene market is expected to grow to USD 173.54 billion by 2032; The global polypropylene market is expected to grow with a CAGR of 4.7% <2> The global polypropylene market was valued at approximately USD 99,276.2 million in 2025 and is projected to experience significant growth, reaching an estimated USD 154,172.9 million by 2035. [2, 3] This expansion represents a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.5% over the forecast period. [2, 3] The primary drivers of this growth are the increasing demand from diverse sectors including packaging, automotive, construction, and healthcare. [2, 3] A notable trend fueling this demand is the rising emphasis on sustainability, which has led to greater adoption of recycled and bio-based polypropylene to comply with environmental regulations and meet consumer preferences for eco-friendly products. [2, 3] <3> In November 2024, North American polypropylene (PP) prices experienced a notable decrease, falling by an average of 3.5 cents per pound. This decline marked the third consecutive month of falling prices, following drops of 6 cents in October and 4 cents in September. The primary drivers for this downward trend were the falling costs of polymer-grade propylene (PGP) feedstock and strategic inventory reduction by producers. Facing weak demand from key sectors like automotive and construction, and increased domestic supply, suppliers focused on lowering their stock levels to avoid year-end tax penalties. This move was also influenced by price competition from international markets, particularly from the Middle East and China. <4> In October 2024, North American polypropylene (PP) resin prices decreased by an average of 6 cents per pound, continuing a downward trend from the previous month. This decline was primarily attributed to falling prices for polymer-grade propylene (PGP) feedstock and a reduction in domestic demand. The market experienced bearish conditions, with PP prices falling approximately 3.2% in the first half of the month, influenced by a corresponding 3.5% drop in PGP feedstock costs. Additional factors contributing to the price depreciation included unfavorable export conditions, as traders focused on liquidating existing inventories rather than restocking. <5> In mid-October 2024, the U.S. polypropylene (PP) market experienced a bearish trend, primarily due to unfavorable export conditions and a decline in production costs. [1] A significant factor in the reduced production costs was the continued drop in prices for feedstock propylene. [1] This price deterioration was intensified by an increase in upstream inventory in September and downward pressure from PGP monomer costs. [1] Consequently, the U.S. PP market struggled to compete with more affordable international offerings from Asia and the Middle East, leading to a notable depreciation in prices. [1] Exports saw minimal interest, with the exception of Mexico, and fell significantly below August levels. [1] Adding to the market dynamics, INEOS resumed production in late October, which further increased domestic supply and contributed to the bearish conditions. [4, 6] By the end of the month, producers' stocks were considerably lower than in March, and many suppliers were focused on depleting existing inventories. [1] <6> Enterprise Products declared a force majeure on October 10, 2024, at its propane dehydrogenation (PDH) facility in Mont Belvieu, Texas, due to technical issues.; On October 13, INVISTA also declared a force majeure at its Houston facility.; These events had the potential to increase production costs for polypropylene. <7> Formosa Plastics Corporation USA officially announced the launch of its new polypropylene (PP) production unit at its Point Comfort, Texas facility on May 17, 2024. [5] The new unit, which is the largest horizontal PP reactor in North America, has an annual production capacity of 550 million pounds and can produce a full slate of PP resins, including homopolymer, random copolymer, and impact copolymer. [2, 5] The plant was once scheduled to begin operating as early as the third quarter of 2021, indicating a significant delay has occurred. [4] The company stated that mechanical work would be completed by the end of May 2024, with the plant's commission and startup scheduled for the third quarter of 2024. [2, 5] <8> Demand for polypropylene (PP) was weak throughout Q4 2023, influenced by factors including surplus supply and high manufacturing costs. Key sectors like construction and automotive experienced subdued demand. The U.S. auto sector, a major consumer of PP, saw a sharp slowdown in the fourth quarter. This followed the resolution of the United Auto Workers (UAW) strike, which began on September 15, 2023, and concluded with tentative deals with Ford, Stellantis, and General Motors on October 25, October 28, and October 30, respectively. While motor vehicle production surged by 7.1% in November after the strike's resolution, the broader manufacturing sector remained challenged by high borrowing costs. The weak overall demand for PP was part of a larger trend of oversupply in Asian and global markets. <9> In the second quarter of 2023, the United States polypropylene (PP) market was characterized by price fluctuations driven by a combination of factors. The period was largely influenced by weak demand from downstream industries and high inventory levels, which exerted downward pressure on prices. [5] New production capacity that came online in late 2022 and early 2023 also contributed to an oversupplied market. [2] Volatility in the cost of polymer-grade propylene (PGP), a primary feedstock, was another significant factor, with a notable price drop in April 2023. [8] Despite the overall weakness, prices saw a low point in June, hitting 46 cents per pound, before beginning an upward trend toward the end of the quarter as market conditions and order numbers started to improve. [8, 5] The automotive sector's performance had a notable impact on demand. [8]

[7, 14] <2> The global polypropylene market is estimated to be valued at USD 125.62 billion in 2025; The global polypropylene market is expected to grow to USD 173.54 billion by 2032; The global polypropylene market is expected to grow with a CAGR of 4.7% <3> The global polypropylene market was valued at approximately USD 99,276.2 million in 2025 and is projected to experience significant growth, reaching an estimated USD 154,172.9 million by 2035. [2, 3] This expansion represents a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 4.5% over the forecast period. [2, 3] The primary drivers of this growth are the increasing demand from diverse sectors including packaging, automotive, construction, and healthcare. [2, 3] A notable trend fueling this demand is the rising emphasis on sustainability, which has led to greater adoption of recycled and bio-based polypropylene to comply with environmental regulations and meet consumer preferences for eco-friendly products. [2, 3] <4> In November 2024, North American polypropylene (PP) prices experienced a notable decrease, falling by an average of 3.5 cents per pound. This decline was primarily attributed to falling prices for polymer-grade propylene (PGP) feedstock and a reduction in domestic demand. The market experienced bearish conditions, with PP prices falling approximately 3.2% in the first half of the month, influenced by a corresponding 3.5% drop in PGP feedstock costs. Additional factors contributing to the price depreciation included unfavorable export conditions, as traders focused on liquidating existing inventories rather than restocking. <6> In mid-October 2024, the U.S. polypropylene (PP) market experienced a bearish trend, primarily due to unfavorable export conditions and a decline in production costs. [1] This price deterioration was intensified by an increase in upstream inventory in September and downward pressure from PGP monomer costs. [1] Consequently, the U.S. PP market struggled to compete with more affordable international offerings from Asia and the Middle East, leading to a notable depreciation in prices. [1] Exports saw minimal interest, with the exception of Mexico, and fell significantly below August levels. [1] Adding to the market dynamics, INEOS resumed production in late October, which further increased domestic supply and contributed to the bearish conditions. [4, 6] By the end of the month, producers' stocks were considerably lower than in March, and many suppliers were focused on depleting existing inventories. [5] The new unit, which is the largest horizontal PP reactor in North America, has an annual production capacity of 550 million pounds and can produce a full slate of PP resins, including homopolymer, random copolymer, and impact copolymer. [2, 5] The plant was once scheduled to begin operating as early as the third quarter of 2021, indicating a significant delay has occurred. [4] The company stated that mechanical work would be completed by the end of May 2024, with the plant's commission and startup scheduled for the third quarter of 2024. [2, 5] <9> Demand for polypropylene (PP) was weak throughout Q4 2023, influenced by factors including surplus supply and high manufacturing costs. Key sectors like construction and automotive experienced subdued demand. The U.S. auto sector, a major consumer of PP, saw a sharp slowdown in the fourth quarter. This followed the resolution of the United Auto Workers (UAW) strike, which began on September 15, 2023, and concluded with tentative deals with Ford, Stellantis, and General Motors on October 25, October 28, and October 30, respectively. While motor vehicle production surged by 7.1% in November after the strike's resolution, the broader manufacturing sector remained challenged by high borrowing costs. These chemicals are derived from plastic waste-based feedstocks and were intended for use in producing products such as transportation fuels. The withdrawal of the proposed SNURs, originally released in June 2023, followed a court's decision on December 4, 2024, which granted a motion from the EPA.
